method: Two read-only LLM agents with the scope the first audit left out, after the static and wiring tests were in. Lifecycle: every spawn, lock, abort, loop and timeout in the core, the three processes and their units, checked against the matrix-sdk 0.19.1 sources on the build host. Untrusted input, privacy and names: every path from other people's servers and other apps into StyledText, links, shares, D-Bus and the log, with Qt 5.6 StyledText and Silica's Label read from source. Findings fixed in small commits, each with a test where one can reach it (I2 and I3 written failing first).

findings.status: FIXED 760903c (re-enable after 30 s and on sync Running; retry_send; discard re-enables)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: after any send error the SDK switches the room's send queue off, and Rustrx switches it back on only for rooms where it dropped a refused reaction. After a network error (recoverable) or a refused message (unrecoverable), every later message in that room stays 'sending' until the app restarts; 'Send again' and 'Discard' do not help.
findings.detail: SDK: on any error in the room's sending task, `locally_enabled.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);` (send_queue/mod.rs:1019). Recoverable (transient HTTP, NetworkFailure, ConcurrentRequestFailed, mod.rs:999-1013): the request is kept, `queue.mark_as_not_being_sent` (mod.rs:1026). Unrecoverable: `queue.mark_as_wedged` (mod.rs:1035), which blocks the room's later requests to keep the order. The task then loops: `if !locally_enabled.load(..) { notifier.notified().await; continue; }` (mod.rs:696-700). A new send, an abort (mod.rs:2864, 2883) or an unwedge (mod.rs:3012) only calls `notifier.notify_one()`; the task wakes, sees the flag still false and sleeps again. The only code that stores true is `RoomSendQueue::set_enabled` (mod.rs:1232-1238) and `SendQueue::set_enabled` (mod.rs:286-297); in the SDK they are called only by `Client::resume` (client/mod.rs:3840). The SyncService does not touch the send queue (no send_queue reference in sync_service.rs), also not when it comes back from Offline. Rustrx: `send_queue_watch` (core/src/core/timeline.rs:14-25) handles `Ok(e) if !e.is_recoverable => Self::drop_refused_reactions(&client).await` and `Ok(_) => {}` (timeline.rs:19-20): a recoverable error is ignored. `drop_refused_reactions` calls `room.send_queue().set_enabled(true)` only for rooms in `woken`, i.e. rooms where an m.reaction was aborted (timeline.rs:41-55); a room whose refused event is a message is not re-enabled. UI: a failed echo is `send_state: "failed"` for both kinds (serialize.rs:571-574, `SendingFailed { .. }`). 'Send again' is `rustrx.command({ cmd: "redact", room_id: page.roomId, txn_id: txnId }); rustrx.sendText(page.roomId, text, "")` (qml/pages/RoomPage.qml:418-421; ThreadPage.qml:151): the redact aborts the echo (notify only), the new text is queued into the still-disabled queue and shows 'sending' forever. 'Discard' (MessageDelegate.qml:728-732) is the same abort. Why a restart helps: a new Client starts with `SendQueueData::new(true)` (client/builder/mod.rs:724), and at start `drop_refused_reactions` calls `client.send_queue().local_echoes()`, which calls `self.for_room(room)` for every room with unsent requests (send_queue/mod.rs:321-338) and so spawns their tasks enabled; that resume is incidental. A wedged message survives a restart and still blocks its room until it is discarded (after a restart Discard then works, because the queue is enabled again).
findings.fix: proposed: (1) in send_queue_watch, on `Ok(e) if e.is_recoverable`, re-enable that room (`client.get_room(&e.room_id).map(|r| r.send_queue().set_enabled(true))`) after a backoff (e.g. 2 s doubling to 60 s, reset on success), and also call `client.send_queue().set_enabled(true).await` whenever the SyncService state goes to Running (sync.rs:55-75 already sees every transition; it also respawns rooms with unsent requests, mod.rs:222-241); for the classic sync, on the first successful `sync` after an error (sync.rs:26-33). (2) A `retry_send {room_id, txn_id}` command that finds the echo in `local_echoes()`, calls `send_handle.unwedge()` when it is wedged, then `room.send_queue().set_enabled(true)`; 'Send again' uses it instead of redact+sendText (keeps the order and the txn id, works for media too). (3) After a Discard of a failed echo (redact with txn_id), call `room.send_queue().set_enabled(true)`. (4) Optionally expose `room.send_queue().is_enabled()` in the timeline event so the UI can show 'paused'.
findings.test: Rust integration test with the SDK's MatrixMockServer (matrix-sdk test-utils) or wiremock: send in a room with the /send endpoint answering a connection reset (recoverable) once, then 200; assert that a second message reaches the mock without a new Client. Second case: answer 400 M_FORBIDDEN (unrecoverable) for a message, discard it, send again, assert it arrives. Phone: airplane mode, send a message, network back, wait for sync 'running': the message must leave; today it stays 'sending' until restart.

findings.status: FIXED cb14789 (login generation; server logout bounded to 15 s; wipe only for the same generation)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED path: logout wipes the store and deletes session.json after an unbounded network await, with nothing tying the wipe to the login it belongs to. A second Logout tap during that wait reports logged_out at once; a login made then has its fresh store and session file deleted when the first logout's network call returns.
findings.detail: session.rs:444-460: `self.call_end().await;` (network: leave_own_memberships, call.rs:273-295), `let teardown = self.state.lock().await.take_login();`, `if let Some(client) = teardown.stop().await { if let Err(e) = client.logout().await {..} }`, then `std::fs::remove_file(self.session_path()).ok(); self.wipe_local_data(); self.emit(json!({"ev": "logged_out"}));`. `client.logout()` uses the default RequestConfig: 30 s per attempt and transient errors retried for up to 15 minutes (http_client/native.rs:56-60, http_client/mod.rs:51). The UI stays logged in until logged_out arrives; the Log out button stays enabled (qml/pages/SettingsPage.qml:354-362, remorse only). A second `logout` finds `client` already None (take_login returns empty), skips the network, wipes, emits logged_out. login_password/login_sso only check `client.is_some()` (session.rs:369, 404), so the user can log in again (same or other account) while the first logout task is still in `client.logout().await`. When it returns, session.rs:457-458 delete the new session.json and `remove_dir_all` the new account's live store (session.rs:303-311), and a second logged_out is emitted. The same unguarded pattern is in session_expired (session.rs:281-300, but its awaits are local).
findings.fix: proposed: a login generation counter in State (the next structural step the first audit named): take_login bumps it and returns it; logout does the local part first (remove session.json, wipe, emit logged_out) and the server logout last, on a request with `RequestConfig::short_retry()` / a short timeout, and only the local part if the generation is still the one it took. Disable the Log out button while a logout is pending.
findings.test: Rust unit test with a mock server whose /logout answers after a delay: send logout twice, then login_password, release the delayed answer, assert the new session file and store still exist. Phone only otherwise: slow network (tc netem), tap Log out twice, log in again.

findings.status: FIXED 36a2609 (activate asked again while the holder is still starting; a failed wait logged)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: the bus name is taken before the D-Bus object exists, and any error answer to `activate` is read as 'the holder is leaving'. A launch while the holder is still starting (or hung) waits 10 s and exits silently; the holder stays.
findings.detail: main.cpp:110 `bus.registerService(kService)` happens before `Rustrx rustrx(dataDir);` (main.cpp:128). The constructor first loads the sailfish-secrets plugin and fetches the store key synchronously on the GUI thread (Rustrx.cpp:107-125; SecretStore.cpp:46-47, 67-68, 101-102: `request.waitForFinished();` with `SystemInteraction`, no timeout of its own, QtDBus default 25 s per call), then `rustrx_start` (Rustrx.cpp:130), and only then `bus.registerObject(Keys::kObjectPath, this, ..)` (Rustrx.cpp:142). A second process meanwhile calls `activate` (main.cpp:116-118, 3 s timeout, Keys.h:115); the answer is UnknownObject (or NoReply if the GUI thread is busy > 3 s), and `takeOver = reply.type() == QDBusMessage::ErrorMessage || ..` (main.cpp:120-121) is true, so it waits in `waitForNameToGo` (10 s, Keys.h:112, main.cpp:50-60) for a holder that never got the request, then `return 0` (main.cpp:123-124) with no message. Cases: the stand-in at session start (post-user-session.target) while the device is not unlocked yet, if sailfish-secrets waits for the unlock (SUSPECTED: not verified what the daemon does before the first unlock); any hung holder (Restart=no in both units, nothing kills it). A crashed holder is fine: the bus drops its names on disconnect.
findings.fix: proposed: register the object path (a small responder that can already answer activate) right after registerService, before the secrets fetch; in main.cpp retry `activate` on UnknownObject/UnknownMethod until a deadline and treat only NoReply/ServiceUnknown/Disconnected as 'leaving'; when waitForNameToGo fails, log it and show a notification instead of exiting silently; give the SecretStore requests a bounded wait.
findings.test: phone only: delay the stand-in's constructor (e.g. a test-only sleep env var before registerObject), start the stand-in, tap the launcher within the delay: today the app does not appear; after the fix it does. A unit test of the main.cpp decision table (error name -> take over / retry) is possible if that logic is moved into a function.

findings.status: FIXED cb14789 (10 min timeout, login_cancel and a Cancel button)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: a single sign-on login that is not completed in the browser waits forever; the login page has no cancel and stays in 'logging in' with both login buttons disabled until the app is restarted.
findings.detail: session.rs:429 `builder.send().await` -> SDK SsoLoginBuilder::send: `let (redirect_url, server_handle) = server_builder.spawn().await?;` then `server_handle.await` (authentication/matrix/login_builder.rs:327-337); the local redirect server has no timeout. Rustrx adds none and has no cancel command (protocol.rs has no such Command). UI: `m_loggingIn = true` (Rustrx.cpp:395) is cleared only by logged_in, login_error or an error for login_sso (Rustrx.cpp:580-595, 689-692); LoginPage disables both buttons on `!rustrx.loggingIn` (LoginPage.qml:173, 202) and only offers 'Open again' and 'Copy link' (LoginPage.qml:211-251). The pending task also holds a Client with the store open (built at session.rs:412) and kept_device may already have wiped a kept store (session.rs:410, 269).
findings.fix: proposed: wrap the SSO send in `tokio::time::timeout` (e.g. 10 min) and add a `login_cancel` command that aborts the pending login task (keep its JoinHandle in State); a Cancel button in the waiting block of LoginPage. Both end in login_error.
findings.test: Rust test: login_sso against a mock server, never call the redirect URL, send login_cancel, assert login_error and that a second login_sso starts. Phone: start SSO, close the browser, press Cancel.

findings.status: FIXED cb14789 (get_media and fetch_emote check the generation before writing)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED path: command tasks are not tied to the login. A media download in flight at logout finishes afterwards and writes the old account's decrypted file into the freshly wiped media folder, and emits a media event.
findings.detail: Every command runs on its own detached task: `self.rt.spawn(async move { if let Err(e) = self.handle(command).await {..} })` (commands.rs:21-25), never aborted. get_media holds the Room/Client it resolved and, after its network awaits (timeline.rs:448-469, SDK default up to 15 min of retries on 5xx), writes `self.data_dir.join(MEDIA_DIR).join(..)` (timeline.rs:499-501) and emits "media" (timeline.rs:502). logout's `wipe_local_data` removes and recreates MEDIA_DIR (session.rs:307-310) before that write can happen. Same for fetch_emote (timeline.rs:536-547, writes media/emotes). The decrypted file of the old account then stays on disk after the logout, against what logout promises ('Everything of the account on this phone', session.rs:302). Other detached tasks hold the old timeline/client briefly but write nothing: open_room's first page (timeline.rs:195-197), fetch_replied (timeline.rs:96-100), the thread's page_in (threads.rs:55-57).
findings.fix: proposed: keep command tasks of the current login in a `JoinSet`/Vec in State (abort on take_login), or capture the login generation at dispatch and check it before every file write and emit in get_media/fetch_emote; simplest: get_media writes to a temp name and renames only if the generation still matches.
findings.test: Rust test with a mock media endpoint that answers after a delay: get_media, logout, release the answer, assert media/ is empty. Phone: open a large picture on a slow link and log out at once.

findings.status: FIXED b1fe4ce (push_handle serialised)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED that concurrent push_handle commands each build their own NotificationClient; SUSPECTED that their encryption syncs then run concurrently over one crypto store (the SDK assumes one per process).
findings.detail: push.rs:82 `let nc = NotificationClient::new(client.clone(), NotificationProcessSetup::MultipleProcesses).await?;` per command, and each command is its own task (commands.rs:21). Pushes queued before login are flushed in one loop (Rustrx.cpp:589-591), later ones arrive per D-Bus call, so a burst gives parallel push_handle tasks. In the SDK the encryption sync is serialised by `self.encryption_sync_mutex` and a dummy permit that is unique 'since we've acquired the encryption_sync_mutex' (notification_client.rs:336-343) - both per NotificationClient instance. Each instance gets its own Client copy over the same crypto store with `CrossProcessLockConfig::multi_process(Self::LOCK_ID)` (notification_client.rs:208-214, client/mod.rs:3583-3617), all with the same lock id, so they do not exclude each other. Possible results (not observed): duplicate one-time-key / to-device processing, M_UNKNOWN_POS on the shared sliding sync connection, a room key processed by one instance not seen by the other's decryption retry.
findings.fix: proposed: one NotificationClient per process, made once (tokio::sync::OnceCell in Core) and reused by every push_handle; or serialise push_handle behind a tokio Mutex. Either keeps the SDK's own mutex meaningful.
findings.test: phone only: send five encrypted messages within a second to a device whose app is closed with push on, and compare the push log (logs/push.log) for UTD notifications / M_UNKNOWN_POS before and after.

findings.status: FIXED b1fe4ce (replaced task aborted), 1f71efd (a close during the build wins, for threads and the thread list)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: open_thread, thread_list, space_open and call_start close the previous one first, then await, then store the new handle by assignment. A close (or a second open) that arrives during the await is lost: the replaced JoinHandle is dropped, which detaches the task instead of aborting it.
findings.detail: open_thread: `self.close_thread().await;` (threads.rs:41), `build_timeline(.., TimelineFocus::Thread ..).await?` (threads.rs:42, a thread focus loads the root and its relations from the server), then `self.state.lock().await.thread = Some(OpenThread {..})` (threads.rs:62). A close_thread processed during the build finds nothing; the thread then stays open in the core with its task streaming thread_timeline (dropped by the UI, Rustrx.cpp:654) until the next open_thread or logout, and `timeline_holding` (threads.rs:169-198) may route reactions in that room through the stale thread timeline. Two overlapping open_thread: the first OpenThread is overwritten and its task is never aborted (only take_login or close_thread abort the stored one). Same pattern: thread_list (threads.rs:70, 110), space_open (spaces.rs ~85-129, `space_lists.insert` returns the old handle, dropped), call_start (call.rs:161, 243 `call = Some(..)`, the old CallSession's driver keeps running), open_room vs close_room (timeline.rs:185-191; narrower: a live-focus build is mostly local).
findings.fix: proposed: when storing, take the previous value and abort it (`if let Some(old) = st.thread.replace(new) { old.task.abort() }`, `if let Some(old) = st.space_lists.insert(..) { old.abort() }`); plus a per-slot sequence number bumped by close_* and checked before storing, so a close during the build wins.
findings.test: Rust test with a mock server delaying /relations: open_thread then close_thread immediately; assert State.thread is None after both complete and no thread_timeline event follows.

findings.area: task lifetimes / login (session.rs, sync.rs, verification.rs, knock.rs, core.rs)
findings.status: FIXED cb14789 (registration checks the generation; finished login tasks pruned)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED structure, SUSPECTED timing: tasks and the SyncService are registered in State after awaits, without checking that the login they belong to is still current. A teardown that runs in between misses them; they are pushed into the next login's state and keep the old client alive and emitting.
findings.detail: after_login sets `st.client` (session.rs:186-189) and only later pushes watch/rooms/sends (session.rs:196-203); start_sync stores the service and its tasks after `SyncService::builder(..).build().await` and `service.start().await` (sync.rs:43-54, 76-81). Also spawn_login_task (core.rs:191-194; called from the verification event handlers verification.rs:217, 226 and verification.rs:377), watch_request's SAS task (verification.rs:292-294), the knock watchers (knock.rs:77-79). The realistic trigger is session_expired: session_watch is spawned at session.rs:196, before start_sync finishes; an UnknownToken on the first request of an expired restore spawns session_expired (session.rs:224) whose take_login (session.rs:283-287) can run before sync.rs:76-81. Then the old SyncService keeps running (401s), its state_task emits sync_state into the logged-out UI, and the leftovers are aborted only at the next logout. Also login_tasks is never pruned: finished verification, SAS and knock handles accumulate per login (trivial memory).
findings.fix: proposed: the login generation counter (see C2): after_login captures it, every registration checks it under the lock and, if it changed, aborts the handle / stops the service instead of storing it. Prune finished handles (`login_tasks.retain(|h| !h.is_finished())`) when pushing.
findings.test: Rust test: restore with a mock server that answers 401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN (soft_logout false) to everything, assert no sync_state event after logged_out and that State.sync_service is None.

findings.status: FIXED 36a2609 (rustrx_shutdown at aboutToQuit before the name goes; handOver stays when StartUnit fails), f2818af (Client::pause closes the stores)
findings.summary: SUSPECTED: nothing stops the core before the bus name is released. The bus name is the only store lock (cross-process lock off), yet the old process's sync and crypto tasks run until the process is gone.
findings.detail: session.rs:111-115: `.cross_process_store_config(CrossProcessLockConfig::SingleProcess)` with the comment that the D-Bus name is the lock. On exit: `~Rustrx` only calls `rustrx_stop()` (Rustrx.cpp:146-151), which only clears LIVE so events are dropped (lib.rs:38-57); the runtime lives in a static OnceLock and is never shut down (lib.rs:59, 151-155). The name goes when QtDBus closes the session connection (during QGuiApplication teardown or at process exit; not verified for Qt 5.6) while the tokio workers may still be inside a sync response or a crypto write. The waiting process polls every 100 ms (main.cpp:54-58) and then opens the store. The window is short (milliseconds); SQLite transactions keep the files consistent, but two OlmMachines on one crypto store for even a moment is what the cross-process lock exists for. Also the stand-in's handOver() quits whether or not StartUnit succeeded (Handover.cpp:108-109: result ignored).
findings.fix: proposed: a `shutdown` command (or a blocking `rustrx_shutdown(timeout_ms)` C function) that stops the SyncService, aborts login tasks and calls `client.pause()` (closes all stores, client/mod.rs:3813-3823), called from aboutToQuit before `bus.unregisterService(kService)` is done explicitly. In handOver(), quit only if startUnit returned true (else stay and log), or leave the quit to the new app's activate call (Rustrx.cpp:221-230).
findings.test: phone only: log the timestamps of 'name released' (old process) and 'store opened' (new process) during a stand-in -> app handover; after the fix the old process logs 'stores closed' before the release.

findings.status: FIXED 0c953c0 (and the same pattern in the member, picture and message pages)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: the core answers every failed command with an error event, but three UI flags wait only for the success event, so one failure leaves them stuck.
findings.detail: paginate_back errors go out as {"ev":"error","cmd":"paginate_back"} (commands.rs:21-25, timeline.rs:233). RoomPage sets `paginating = true` (RoomPage.qml:272) and clears it only in `onPaginated` (RoomPage.qml:151); there is no onErrorOccurred in RoomPage, so after one failed page (no network while scrolling up) older history never loads again in that page and the spinner stays (RoomPage.qml:331-335). SearchPage: `page.searching = true` (SearchPage.qml:40), cleared only in onSearchResults (SearchPage.qml:53); its onErrorOccurred clears `pending` only (SearchPage.qml:72). harbour-rustrx.qml:318 `pendingDm = true` before create_dm; on error it stays true and the next unrelated `joined` or `dm_ready` opens that room (harbour-rustrx.qml:336-337).
findings.fix: proposed: RoomPage/ThreadPage: `onErrorOccurred: if (cmd === "paginate_back") paginating = false`; SearchPage: clear `searching` for cmd "search"; harbour-rustrx.qml: clear pendingDm on error for "create_dm". Longer term the error code field the first audit proposed.
findings.test: QML test (qmltestrunner) with a fake rustrx object emitting errorOccurred("paginate_back", ..) and checking `paginating`; or phone: airplane mode, scroll up, network back, scroll up again.

findings.status: FIXED b1fe4ce (catch_unwind in dispatch answers with an error event)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED: a panic inside a command task is contained by tokio but answers nothing: no error event, so the UI waits as in C10. A panic in a login task (rooms_task, encryption_task, send_queue_watch) ends it silently; nothing notices.
findings.detail: Cargo.toml [profile.release] `panic = "unwind"`; the hook logs it (lib.rs:147-150). dispatch spawns `self.handle(command).await` and maps only `Err` to an error event (commands.rs:21-25); a panic unwinds out of the future and the JoinHandle (dropped) carries it. Login tasks' handles are only aborted, never awaited (core.rs:138-146), so a panicked rooms_task leaves the room list frozen with no sign but the log line. No reachable panic site was found (see CN6), so this is defence in depth. Across the C ABI: rustrx_command's synchronous part (lib.rs:161-174, dispatch's parse at commands.rs:9-20) has no panic site; an unwind out of an `extern "C"` fn aborts the process on Rust >= 1.81.
findings.fix: proposed: in dispatch, `AssertUnwindSafe(self.handle(command)).catch_unwind().await` (FutureExt is already imported, core.rs:13) and emit {"ev":"error","cmd":..,"message":"internal error"} on a panic; a supervisor that awaits the login tasks' handles and logs/restarts rooms_task if it ends with a panic.
findings.test: Rust unit test: a test-only command that panics; assert an error event arrives.

findings.status: FIXED 36a2609 (ready says restore_failed; the stand-in exits with a failure, Restart=on-failure RestartSec=60)
findings.summary: SUSPECTED: if the stand-in starts before sailfish-secrets can give the store key (before the first unlock), restore fails once and is never retried; the stand-in then runs logged out, holding the bus name, with no notifications until something restarts it.
findings.detail: session.rs:82-83 bails 'the encrypted store's key is not available'; boot() runs once (session.rs:13-31) and emits ready logged_in:false; STORE_KEY is a OnceLock set once before start (lib.rs:90-108, Rustrx.cpp:111-125). Nothing in Service.qml or main.cpp quits or retries on a logged-out stand-in (main.cpp:158-159 just runs the loop). Whether sailfish-secrets returns an error or blocks before the first unlock was not verified (if it blocks, see C3 instead).
findings.fix: proposed: the stand-in quits when ready says logged_in:false with a restore error, and its unit gets `Restart=on-failure` with a RestartSec (exit non-zero in that case); or retry the key and restore on a timer / on the device lock state changing to unlocked.
findings.test: phone only: reboot with background mode on and push off, do not unlock for a minute, unlock, send a message from another account: a notification must arrive.

findings.area: thread hop at process exit (lib.rs, Rustrx.cpp)
findings.status: FIXED 36a2609 (the core stopped before exit)
findings.summary: CONFIRMED but harmless today: Emitter::emit checks LIVE and then calls the callback without a lock, so a tokio thread can be inside eventCallback while main() returns and static destructors run.
findings.detail: lib.rs:43-50 load LIVE then `(self.cb)(..)`; ~Rustrx sets LIVE false under s_lock (Rustrx.cpp:146-151). A thread that passed the check blocks on s_lock, then sees s_instance null and returns (Rustrx.cpp:320-323) - correct while the process lives. After main returns, the static QMutex s_lock and Qt's globals are destroyed while tokio workers still run (the runtime is never shut down); QJsonDocument::fromJson runs before the lock (Rustrx.cpp:317). No crash has been seen.
findings.fix: proposed: the shutdown in C9 (runtime stopped before exit) removes it; or a reader-count/RwLock in the Emitter so rustrx_stop waits for callbacks in flight.
findings.test: none practical; covered by C9's change.

findings.status: FIXED 4a5290d (Labels plain by default), 634beaa (QML engines without network)
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED (code + Silica and Qt sources; not reproduced on a phone)
findings.summary: Silica Label defaults to Text.AutoText, so every Label without textFormat that shows a remote string renders it as StyledText when it looks like HTML: a display name such as `Bob ` makes the phone fetch that address each time the row is drawn, with no tap.
findings.detail: Silica Label.qml (SFOS 5.1 rootfs, /usr/lib64/qt5/qml/Sailfish/Silica/Label.qml): `textFormat: _defaultLabelFormat`; ApplicationWindow.qml:108 `property int _defaultLabelFormat: Text.AutoText`; Rustrx never overrides it. Qt qquicktext.cpp:1851 `d->styledText = d->format == StyledText || (d->format == AutoText && Qt::mightBeRichText(n))`; Qt 5.6 qtextdocument.cpp Qt::mightBeRichText (read on the 5.6 branch) scans the first line to the first '<', reads the tag name and returns `QTextHtmlParser::lookupElement(tag.toLower()) != -1`, so `Bob ` is rich text (img, a, font, b... are known). StyledText takes any URL (qquickstyledtext.cpp 5.6 `image->url = QUrl(attr.second.toString())`) and QQuickText loads it through QQuickPixmap with the engine's network access (qquicktext.cpp:1325, `imageDownloadFinished`); no QQmlNetworkAccessManagerFactory is installed (grep NetworkAccess: only UnifiedPush's own QNAM) and the app has the Internet permission. Remote strings in AutoText Labels: MessageDelegate.qml:275 `text: model.sender_name || model.sender || ""` (every message from anyone in the room), :244 membership/state line `model.body` (core-built, contains display names and room names), :403 media placeholder `model.body`, :437 poll answer `modelData.text`, :361-365 file/audio name (the body Label's textFormat is PlainText only when htmlText is empty, fine); KnockPage.qml:91 `item.request.name`, :120 `item.request.reason` (anyone may knock), :104/:107 room_name via qsTrId().arg; JoinPage.qml:138 preview name, :165 `page.preview.topic` (a room seen only through a link); SpacePage.qml:118,130,185; RoomInfoPage.qml:160,228,267 (`info.topic`); ThreadsPage.qml:78 `row.t.root.sender_name`; CoverPage.qml:140,162; PageHeader titles/descriptions with room names (RoomPage.qml:172, ThreadPage.qml:161, MembersPage.qml:75, ThreadsPage.qml:54). What leaks: the phone's IP address, the time the row was shown (read tracking), which room. The README/renderHtml comment claims 'a message cannot make the phone fetch from any address'; through the names it can.
findings.fix: Two layers. (1) Set `_defaultLabelFormat: Text.PlainText` on the ApplicationWindow (harbour-rustrx.qml) so every Label is plain unless it says StyledText; check each Label that relies on AutoText (the about lines already set StyledText). (2) Defence in depth: install a QQmlNetworkAccessManagerFactory on both engines (app and Service.qml) whose QNAM refuses every non-file, non-image:// request, since the app never shows remote pictures through QML (avatars, media and emotes are cached files).
findings.test: QML test (qmltestrunner with Silica stubs, or on the phone): a MessageDelegate with sender_name `` and a local HTTP listener; assert no request arrives. Unit level: a C++ test that the factory's QNAM returns an error reply for http(s) URLs.

findings.status: FIXED d54a44c (text between tags escaped; tests written failing first in 2dfb481)
findings.summary: renderHtml lets a tag through when a space follows the '<': `< img src="https://t.example/p.png">` and `< a href="javascript:x">` bypass the tag filter, the image filter and the scheme filter, because the text between tags is never escaped and StyledText skips the space.
findings.detail: src/TimelineModel.cpp:287 `tagRe("<(/?)([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*)([^>]*)>")` needs a letter right after '<', so `< img ...>` stays in the text segment; the `text` lambda (:303-325) only decodes numeric entities and never escapes a literal '<'; emitText -> Twemoji::inHtml (Twemoji.cpp:165) passes `<[^>]*>` through unchanged. Qt 5.6 qquickstyledtext.cpp parseTag begins with `skipSpace(ch);` (checked on the 5.6 branch and in the local 6.11.3 source), so StyledText reads `< img src=...>` as an img tag and loads it (see I1 for the fetch) and `< a href=...>` as a link with any scheme. Same for reply quotes (renderReply -> renderHtml). The emojify path from QML is not affected (callers escape '<' first).
findings.fix: In the text lambda, escape every '<' (and '>' for symmetry) left in a text segment: all real tags were consumed by tagRe, so any '<' still there is text. One line at the top of the lambda, BEFORE its early `if (!seg.contains('&')) return seg;` (otherwise a segment without '&' skips it): `seg.replace('<', "<")` (the decoder already maps < to <).
findings.test: For the renderHtml unit tests being written: input `< img src="https://x/p.png">` must give no 'x` must give no '` likewise; regression guard `<img src=x>` must stay text (`<img src=x>`).

findings.status: FIXED d54a44c (hrefSafe), c735bd7 (one gate for external links)
findings.summary: A quote inside a link address injects a second href that StyledText takes (last href wins, either quote ends a value), so a link that looks like https can open any scheme on tap (file:, sms:, tel:, javascript:, anything a handler is registered for). Worst in plain bodies, which anyone can send.
findings.detail: Plain text path: Twemoji.cpp:209 linkEnd stops only at white space or '<', StyledText::escaped (:216) does not escape '"', linkified (:243) writes ``. Body `https://a"href="file:///etc/passwd"` becomes ``; StyledText parseAnchorAttributes loops over attributes and calls setAnchorHref for each href, parseValue ends a value at either quote, so the href is file:///etc/passwd. HTML path: TimelineModel.cpp:395 replaces '"' with %22 but not "'": `x` passes schemeRe (starts with https) and yields href file:///etc/passwd. The sinks: MessageDelegate.qml:350 and :473 `onLinkActivated: app.openLink(link)`; harbour-rustrx.qml:365-366 `if (!openMatrixUri(link)) Qt.openUrlExternally(link)`, no scheme check at the sink. What file:// opens from inside sailjail (another app's viewer) was not tested.
findings.fix: Percent-encode both quote characters (and '<', '>', whitespace) in the href in both linkified and renderHtml (QUrl::toPercentEncoding with a safe set, or replace '"' -> %22 and '\'' -> %27); stop linkEnd at '"' too. And check the scheme at the sink: openLink opens only http, https, mailto, magnet externally (matrix: stays in the app), everything else is dropped.
findings.test: Unit: linkified(`https://a"href="file:///p"`) must contain exactly one href and it must start with https://a; renderHtml(`x`) must not contain an unencoded "'" inside the href. A QML/JS test for openLink with file:/javascript:/sms: inputs asserting Qt.openUrlExternally is not called.

findings.summary: Three StyledText Labels build markup from remote strings without escaping: the sender's name in a reply quote, and a room's or space's topic in the room list. Same effect as I1 (remote image fetch, fake formatting), and the room list is drawn at start.
findings.detail:
MessageDelegate.qml:330-331 `var who = r.sender_name || r.sender || ""` then `"" + who + "
" + quoted` in a `textFormat: Text.StyledText` Label (:313). RoomDelegate.qml:294 `if (model.is_space) return model.topic ... .replace(/\s+/g, " ")` and :306 `if (model.topic && model.topic.length) return model.topic.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` in the preview Label with `textFormat: Text.StyledText` (:284); the whitespace fold even turns `

findings.status: FIXED c735bd7 (a dialog before a link starts a direct chat)
findings.summary: A tapped matrix:u/ or matrix.to/#/@user link creates a direct chat with that user at once and invites them, without asking: anyone who gets a link tapped (in a message, or on a web page handed to Rustrx through the desktop file's matrix: handler, or by any session-bus client calling openUrl) learns the tapper's Matrix id and gets a DM room.
findings.detail: harbour-rustrx.qml openMatrixUri: `if (id.charAt(0) === "@") { pendingDm = true; rustrx.command({ cmd: "create_dm", user_id: id }) }`; core rooms.rs:73-79 `match client.get_dm_room(&user) { Some(r) => r, None => client.create_dm(&user).await? }` (create_dm makes the room and invites). Entry points: openLink (message links), Rustrx::openUrl (Rustrx.cpp:200, D-Bus net.mowerk.harbour_rustrx.openUrl, the desktop file's `MimeType=x-scheme-handler/matrix`), route() on a cold start (harbour-rustrx.qml:143-144). Rooms and aliases go to JoinPage, which asks first; only users do not.
findings.fix: Show the user (profile name, id, 'Start chat') on a page first, as JoinPage does for rooms; send create_dm only from that page's button.
findings.test: QML test: openMatrixUri("matrix:u/eve:example.org") must push a page and must not call rustrx.command with create_dm.

findings.status: FIXED c735bd7 (geo: only)
findings.summary: A location message's geo_uri goes to Qt.openUrlExternally unchecked: a message can carry any URI as its 'location', shown as 'Location (tap to open)'.
findings.detail: core/src/serialize.rs:392 `put(o, "geo_uri", l.geo_uri.as_str())` (no check); MessageDelegate.qml:148 `Qt.openUrlExternally(model.geo_uri)   // a maps app (Pure Maps) takes geo:`. The visible label is the body, not the URI (MessageDelegate.qml:369).

findings.test: QML/JS: a location item with geo_uri `https://x` or `file:///x` must not reach Qt.openUrlExternally.

findings.area: untrusted input / external URLs from the server
findings.status: FIXED c735bd7 (openExternal: https, http, mailto, geo)
findings.summary: URLs the homeserver hands over are opened without a scheme check: the SSO page (open_url), the identity-reset approval page, the sign-up URL.
findings.detail: Rustrx.cpp:683-686 `open_url` -> browserUrl -> harbour-rustrx.qml:212 `onBrowserUrl: Qt.openUrlExternally(url)` with no user action; SettingsPage.qml:468 resetApprovalUrl; LoginPage.qml:240/274. The SSO URL is built by the SDK from the homeserver address (https), so the realistic risk is a hostile homeserver for identity_reset/signup only. Rustrx adds nothing else to the SDK's SSO flow (session.rs:403-442: localhost listener in the SDK, the token never reaches Rustrx code or a log).
findings.fix: One `openExternal(url)` helper that only passes https (and http for localhost SSO, if ever needed), used by every Qt.openUrlExternally call, including openLink (I3) and geo_uri (I6).
findings.test: grep test in CI: no Qt.openUrlExternally outside the helper.

findings.status: FIXED 8409035 (own folders refused, 512 MB cap, old copies pruned)
findings.summary: A string resource in a share is taken as a local path to any file Rustrx can read, including its own session.json (access and refresh tokens), and the share page shows only its base name; fd copies have no size cap and run on the GUI thread; shared copies are never deleted.
findings.detail: ShareAdaptor.cpp:44-53 `const QString path = Rustrx::localPath(r.toString()); if (QFileInfo(path).isFile()) files << path;` (any path, no check that it lies in a user folder); SharePage.qml:53 shows `files[0].split("/").pop()`. session.rs:145-169 writes the session (tokens) to the data folder, mode 0600 but readable by the app itself, so a caller that cannot read it can ask Rustrx to send it, if the user then picks a room. copyFromDescriptor (:89-111) loops `while (!in.atEnd())` with no limit (a pipe or /dev/zero fills the cache) inside the D-Bus slot on the GUI thread. Nothing removes cache/shared (grep kSharedDir: only ShareAdaptor), so every shared photo stays as a copy. Names: `QFileInfo(name).fileName()` (:79, :94) blocks traversal (non-finding IN6); same names overwrite each other.
findings.fix: Accept string paths only under the user's media folders (Pictures, Videos, Music, Documents, Downloads) and never under the app's own data/config/cache folders; cap fd copies (e.g. the server's upload limit) and copy off the GUI thread; delete cache/shared files after sending or at start.
findings.test: Unit: share({resources:["<AppDataLocation>/session.json"]}) must not yield it in files; an fd to /dev/zero must stop at the cap.

findings.status: FIXED 837a499 in part: key and session commands refused through dev; the hook stays in test builds by design
findings.summary: dev() is compiled into release builds and gated only by a file in the data folder; once the file is there, any process that can reach the session bus name can run every core command, e.g. export_keys with its own path and passphrase, or read the room list.
findings.detail: Rustrx.h:342 `Q_SCRIPTABLE QString dev(const QString &json);` (no #ifdef); Rustrx.cpp:327-331 checks `QFile::exists(flag)` only, then `command(req)` for any `cmd`. No package creates the flag (comment Rustrx.h:336), and sailjailed apps cannot write the data folder, so the exposure is a phone where the flag was left behind after testing.
findings.fix: Compile dev() only in debug builds (or behind a CONFIG flag the release spec does not set), and refuse export_keys/import_keys/logout/delete_device there even in debug.
findings.test: Build check: `nm`/`strings` on the release binary must not contain the dev method name; or a unit test that the release Q_CLASSINFO introspection lacks it.

findings.status: FIXED c721905 (no connector call without a stored token)
findings.summary: The UnifiedPush connector compares the caller's token with the stored one, but after a logout (and before the first Register) the stored token is empty, so a call with no token passes: any session-bus client can set the endpoint, which the next login then registers as the pusher (with a gateway probed from that host) until the distributor's own NewEndpoint replaces it.
findings.detail: UnifiedPush.cpp:186-197 loggedOut `m_state.clear()` (token gone); :293 `if (args.value("token").toString() != m_state.value("token").toString()) return` passes for "" == ""; same in unregistered (:312) and message (:327). newEndpoint stores the endpoint (https only); loggedIn -> registerApp (new token) -> setPusherIfNeeded uses the stored endpoint and discoverGateway probes its host (:263-282). The connector is exported in every process, whether push is on or not (main.cpp:132 `rustrx.push()->exportConnector();`), so the empty-token window is open whenever no token is stored. What leaks while it lasts: room and event ids, unread counts, times (docs/PUSH.md 'What leaves the phone').
findings.fix: Refuse every connector call while the stored token is empty, and compare tokens only when both are non-empty.
findings.test: Unit: UnifiedPush with empty state; newEndpoint({token:"", endpoint:"https://evil"}) must leave the endpoint empty.

findings.status: FIXED c5f8de8 (one capped, masked forward; origin check), 8409035 (shared file names out of the log); matrix-sdk WARN lines not read
findings.summary: The claim 'room and user ids, never message texts or passwords' holds for Rustrx's own lines, with three gaps: Element Call's own error and warning text goes into the log (third-party text, up to 600-800 characters, which can carry names, URLs and tokens Element Call chose to print); any frame of any origin in the call WebView can write lines through the `rustrx-console` event, without the 2000-line cap; and shared files are logged by name.
findings.detail: call-bridge.js:86-90 listener for the page's `rustrx-console` CustomEvent: no origin check (unlike the message listener at :103), no count limit (the cap `sent++ > 2000` is only in forward(), :128); :115-140 console-api-log-event and nsIScriptError observers forward page text; CallPage.qml:89-90 `console.log("call page", data.level + ":", data.text)` -> DebugLog. ShareAdaptor.cpp:110 `qInfo() << "share: received" << file`. Checked clean: all 72 tracing calls in core/src (ids, counts, error text), commands.rs:12 (cmd and room id), Rustrx.cpp:381-383 (command name only, password never), UnifiedPush.cpp:301 (endpoint size only, never the endpoint), CallPage.qml:60-67 (widget api/action only), CallPage.qml:73 (URL cut at '?'), the SSO URL is never logged. Not checked: what matrix-sdk logs at WARN (default filter lib.rs:131 `warn,rustrx=info,...`; tools/run-on-phone.sh raises it to info for tests).
findings.fix: Forward Element Call's lines only when a debug switch for calls is on, or only their first 120 characters with URLs and long base64 runs masked; check origin (`e.target.ownerGlobal.location.origin === ORIGIN`) and the cap in the rustrx-console listener; log shared files by size only. State in the README that the log can hold Element Call's own messages during a call.
findings.test: JS test of call-bridge with a fake window: a rustrx-console event from another origin must not reach sendAsyncMessage; the 2001st must be dropped.

findings.status: FIXED 7190dfd (threadsSeen at logout), 30e7ec3 (drafts in the SDK store, old ones moved at login)
findings.summary: Drafts (message text being typed) are kept in the plain QSettings file, outside the encrypted store, and the per-thread seen counts (keyed by event id) survive a logout.
findings.detail: Rustrx.cpp:542-548 setDraft -> `m_settings.setValue("drafts/<room id>", text)` in ~/.config/net.mowerk/harbour-rustrx/harbour-rustrx.conf (Rustrx.cpp:57-60); the store is encrypted with the sailfish-secrets key (session.rs:58-95) but this file is not. Logout removes drafts (Rustrx.cpp:621) and RoomLists::clear removes invitesNotified (RoomLists.cpp:377-380, the first audit's 458f9ad), but nothing removes `threadsSeen/*` (Rustrx.cpp:437-455).
findings.fix: Either keep drafts in the core's store (encrypted) or say in Settings that drafts are stored unencrypted; remove threadsSeen at logout with the drafts.
findings.test: After a logout event, the settings file must contain no drafts/ or threadsSeen/ keys.

findings.status: FIXED 99bc45a (unread from the server's read receipts; the UI's own counts removed)
findings.summary: Thread 'new' counts are the UI's own: a reply count saved per thread in QSettings, beside the SDK's threaded read receipt that the same page sends. Reading a thread in another client never clears Rustrx's count, and the first time a thread is seen all its replies count as read; threadSeen() writes settings from inside a binding.
findings.detail: MessageDelegate.qml:46-47 and ThreadsPage.qml:60 `Math.max(0, count - rustrx.threadSeen(root, count))`; Rustrx.cpp:437-445 threadSeen stores `count` when the key is missing (a write from a binding evaluation); ThreadPage.qml:49-50 `rustrx.markThreadSeen(...)` and `rustrx.command({ cmd: "mark_thread_read" })` both. The SDK knows the thread's unread state from receipts (matrix-sdk-ui thread summaries / read receipts).
findings.fix: Take the thread's unread count from the core (thread receipts) and drop threadsSeen; if kept, make threadSeen read-only and set the baseline where the thread is first listed.
findings.test: Core test: after a threaded receipt from another device the thread_list entry reports 0 new; UI shows the core's number.

findings.area: distrust / notification counts and push state
findings.status: FIXED 05a39c2 (the room's own count, closed when read elsewhere; push_check at login)
findings.summary: Two more UI-kept claims: the notification's 'N new messages' is a counter in Service.qml that only grows until the notification closes, apart from the SDK's unread/notification counts; and UnifiedPush's 'active' trusts a pusherSet flag saved once and never checked against the server's pusher list.
findings.detail: Service.qml:91-93 `var pending = (roomPending[roomId] || 0) + count` and :219-221 (push path); reset only in closeNotification (:256-258). A room read on another device keeps its banner and count until the next local action. UnifiedPush.cpp:96-99 active() = enabled && pusherSet && endpoint; pusherSet is set in pusherSet() (:247-255) and cleared only by a new endpoint, logout or off; a server that dropped the pusher (password change, admin, expiry) is not noticed.
findings.fix: Notifications: take the count from the room's notifications/unread when it changes and close the banner when it reaches 0. Push: at login, list the pushers (client.pusher / GET /pushers) and clear pusherSet when ours is missing.
findings.test: Integration: mark a room read from another client; the banner must go. Delete the pusher server side; after restart status must not say active.

findings.status: FIXED 448a5f2 (every field documented), 48d544f (protocol 2: room_or_alias, mxc, recovery_key, member_count, avatar_path, thread_root, latest_sender_name)
findings.summary: Wire names are consistent snake_case and QML/C++ locals camelCase, but several names mean two things on the wire, and a few concepts have two names in one layer (see name_table).
findings.detail: One name, two things: `id` = room id or alias (room_preview, knock, join_by_id_or_alias, protocol.rs:107-109) vs the timeline item's row id (`id`, PROTOCOL.md timeline item) vs a poll answer id; `url` = an mxc address (send_sticker protocol.rs:39, add_user_emote :93, image pack images) vs an https page (open_url, call_url, identity_reset_approval) while fetch_emote/emote say `mxc` and space_rooms/room_preview say `avatar_mxc`; `key` = a reaction key (react) vs a recovery key (recovery_recover, recovery_key); `avatar` = a cached file path in the room object vs `avatar_mxc` elsewhere; `members` = a count (search_results, room_preview, space_rooms) vs a list (members event); `state` = membership (room object), sync state, verification, recovery, sas. Two names, one thing: thread root is `root` (open_thread, thread_timeline, thread_list) and `thread_root` (send_text, send_sticker, timeline item) on the wire, `root`/`rootId`/`threadRoot`/`m_threadRoot` in QML/C++; user id is `user_id`, `sender`, `other_user`, `inviter`, `latest_sender` (a display name there, not an id: serialize.rs:455-456 `let who = profile_name(&latest.sender_profile, &latest.sender); put(&mut t, "latest_sender", who)`); space id is `space_id` and `parent` (create_room's parent, CreateRoomPage.qml:45, missing from PROTOCOL.md's create_room row together with `space` and `join_rule`); room id is `rid` only in call.rs:226-244 and threads.rs.
findings.fix: Pick one wire name per concept for protocol 2 (thread_root everywhere, mxc for every mxc address, room_or_alias for id, recovery_key for the key) and add the missing create_room fields to PROTOCOL.md now.
findings.test: protocol.rs already has a field test (COMMANDS list); extend it with a deny-list: no field named `url` whose value starts with mxc://, no `id` on room commands.

findings.status: FIXED 229f4e3, 16d1056, d13ed49 (dconf path in names.js), 4d8f277 (the call origin tested against the core's address)
findings.summary: Values defined twice, or as literals beside their constant: the bus name/path/interface in Service.qml, the Element Call origin in Rust and JS, a third spelling of the app id, the page size in QML and Rust, a menu delay literal, the dconf base path in eight files, and core names outside consts.rs.
findings.detail: Service.qml:66-68 `"net.mowerk.harbour-rustrx"`, `"/net/mowerk/harbour_rustrx"`, `"net.mowerk.harbour_rustrx"` duplicate Keys.h kBusName/kObjectPath/kInterface (could come from a rustrx property); call.rs:26 `ELEMENT_CALL_URL = "https://call.element.io/room"` vs call-bridge.js:9 `ORIGIN = "https://call.element.io"` (nothing checks they agree; a self-hosted Element Call later would break the origin check silently); call.rs:200 `ClientProperties::new("net.mowerk.rustrx", ...)` vs push.rs:14 `APP_ID = "net.mowerk.harbour_rustrx"` vs kInterface; Tunables.qml:88 `paginateBatch: 30` sent explicitly by RoomPage.qml:273 while consts.rs PAGINATE_DEFAULT = 30 (two sources since 118cc80); RoomPage.qml:135 `interval: 350` = Tunables.menuCloseMs (350, 'menu closed'); `/apps/harbour-rustrx` in Settings.qml:25 plus 8 debug ConfigurationValues (ChatTrace.qml:55-56, MainPage.qml:46-48, VoicePage.qml:63, harbour-rustrx.qml:450,453); consts.rs says 'tunables and fixed names in one place' but ELEMENT_CALL_URL, WIDGET_ID (call.rs:26-27), APP_ID (push.rs:14), DEVICE_NAME, USER_AGENT (core.rs:62-63) and the event type strings live in their files; kPushIdleMs/kPushMaxLifeMs equal RING_LIFETIME_* by coincidence (commented in Keys.h:118-120, fine). dbus/net.mowerk.harbour_rustrx.service declares `Name=net.mowerk.harbour-rustrx` (file name and bus name differ; the session bus accepts it).
findings.fix: Expose kBusName/kObjectPath/kInterface to QML as constants; pass the call origin to the page (CallPage property set from call_url's origin) instead of a JS literal; one app id constant per layer, named after kInterface; drop paginateBatch (send no count) or drop the core default; use Tunables.menuCloseMs; one Settings path constant for the debug keys.
findings.test: A repo grep check (tools/): each literal on a deny-list appears exactly once outside Keys.h/consts.rs/Tunables.qml.

findings.status: DECIDED: documented design (docs/CALLS.md); Element Call is trusted with the capabilities it asks for
findings.summary: The Element Call page is loaded from call.element.io at call time and its widget gets every capability it asks for; the origin check in the bridge only keeps other origins out, it does not limit what that page can make the driver do in the room.
findings.detail: docs/CALLS.md:41-42 'every capability Element Call asks for is granted'; call-bridge.js:103 `if (!content || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;` and :124 `content.postMessage(..., ORIGIN)` (both correct). CallPage.qml sets global WebEngine prefs (autoplay) at :34-39 for every WebView in the process.

non_findings.what: State lock: one tokio::sync::Mutex (core.rs:153), no std::sync / parking_lot lock anywhere in the core, so no lock ordering and no std guard across an await. Every `.lock().await` was checked; each guard is a temporary or a block that ends before the next network/long await: core.rs:182, 193; session.rs:187, 203, 283-287, 369, 404, 451; sync.rs:35, 76-78, 81; timeline.rs:179, 187-192 (explicit drop), 202, 220, 404; threads.rs:62, 110, 115, 123, 138, 148, 171; spaces.rs:83, 89-93, 129, 134; knock.rs:77-79; verification.rs:51 (block), 119, 160, 164, 250-255, 292-294 (spawn only); call.rs:243, 251-256 (holds across `handle.send`, which is synchronous: `pub fn send(&self, message: String) -> bool`, widget/mod.rs:120), 260. The open_room fix of the first audit is complete.

Thread hop: eventCallback (Rustrx.cpp:314-325) parses on the calling thread, then under s_lock checks s_instance and posts handleEvent with Qt::QueuedConnection; every QObject access (models, signals, m_settings, DebugLog via qInfo) happens in handleEvent on the GUI thread (Rustrx.cpp:551-745), including log lines ('log' events, Rustrx.cpp:554-562). The callback also fires synchronously on the GUI thread from rustrx_command (dispatch logs 'command', commands.rs:12), which is fine: the queued post does not re-enter, and s_lock is only held by the destructor, which does not call into the core except rustrx_stop. m_handleEvent and s_instance are written before rustrx_start creates the worker threads (Rustrx.cpp:70, 126-130): happens-before via thread creation.

DebugLog: the Qt message handler may run on any Qt thread; appendLine and collect take a recursive QMutex (DebugLog.cpp:31, 44, 111); s_path/s_previous are written once in install() before other threads exist. Thread-safe. FrameStats (debug only) counts on the render thread with atomics and reads on the GUI thread (FrameStats.cpp:40-66): fine.
Events cannot be lost to NUL bytes: Emitter::emit drops the event if CString::new fails (lib.rs:47), but serde_json escapes U+0000 as \u0000, so a serialized Value never contains a raw NUL.

Network awaits never hang forever by themselves: every SDK request has a 30 s per-attempt timeout (http_client/mod.rs:51) and transient retries end after 15 minutes total (http_client/native.rs:56-60); network failures are not retried without a retry limit (native.rs:133-138). The exception is the SSO redirect wait (C4). No command holds the state lock across these awaits (CN1).

Panic sites in the core are all guarded: lib.rs:85 expect (only after start), lib.rs:113 unwrap on a constant; account.rs:109 `ids[0]` of a one-element array; packs.rs:47 `out[0]` after `if out.is_empty() { return None }`; packs.rs:191 `as_object_mut().unwrap()` after `if !v.is_object() { v = json!({}) }`; serialize.rs:152 slices at a char_indices boundary; call.rs:109 `lifetime - age` after `if age >= lifetime { return }`. protocol.rs index/asserts are in tests.

Logout teardown (first audit's fix, 458cd54/bc532d9) is complete for what is stored in State: take_login (core.rs:112-135) collects login_tasks, the open room, sync task, call (stopped), requests/sas, thread, thread list, space service and space lists; Teardown::stop aborts them and stops the SyncService outside the lock (core.rs:137-147). The verification watchers are login tasks now (verification.rs:217, 226, 294, 377). What remains is registration after teardown (C8), replaced-not-aborted handles (C7) and command tasks (C5).

Late events after logged_out from aborted tasks: abort takes effect at the task's next await; logout emits logged_out only after `service.stop().await` and the network logout, session_expired after `service.stop().await` (session.rs:290, 299), so an aborted task would need one poll longer than those awaits. Events already queued before logged_out are delivered before it (one Qt event queue, FIFO), and logged_out clears the models (Rustrx.cpp:596-625).

Crash while holding the bus name: the bus daemon releases a name when the owner's connection closes, so a crashed or killed process frees the lock at once and the next start proceeds (main.cpp:110, 123). Only a hung holder blocks (C3).

Push wake never opens the store beside another Rustrx: it exits if push is off (main.cpp:99-100), if any process has the connector name (main.cpp:101-102), or if the bus name is taken (main.cpp:110-113: `if (pushWake) return 0;`). A launcher start while push wake runs makes it quit through activate (Rustrx.cpp:221-230) and waits for its name. The stand-in exits at once when push is active (main.cpp:94-95).

Handover file ordering: the stand-in writes the file before StartUnit (Handover.cpp:97-108); the new app reads and removes it only after it owns the bus name (main.cpp:133-134, Handover.cpp:113-126), so it never reads a half-written file from a live writer.

Spawned loops that end: session_watch breaks on Closed and after UnknownToken (session.rs:212-230); rooms_task breaks on Closed (sync.rs:113-119); the SyncService state task ends with the stream (sync.rs:57-64); encryption_task's select has `else => break` (sync.rs:283-295); send_queue_watch breaks on Closed (timeline.rs:22); verification/SAS watchers end on Done/Cancelled (verification.rs:300-315, 343-351); thread/space/knock/call forwarders end with their streams. The classic sync loop (sync.rs:26-33) loops forever with a 5 s pause on error by design and is aborted on logout. No task swallows errors silently except those that log at info (thread list, space list, avatars, emotes), which is intended.

Every command ends in either its answering event, an intended silent Ok (send_*/react/redact/edit: the timeline update is the answer; fetch_emote failures are logged on purpose, timeline.rs:534-541; mark_thread_read with no thread), or {"ev":"error","cmd":..} via dispatch (commands.rs:21-25) - including login_password/login_sso, which answer login_error (session.rs:394-400, 435-441). Unparsable commands get an error event before anything runs (commands.rs:13-19). The gaps are UI-side (C10) and panics (C11).
renderHtml decodes numeric entities to text and re-escapes <, >, & (TimelineModel.cpp:316-322): `<img src=x>` stays text.
renderHtml drops every non-mxc (keeps alt with '<' escaped) and emits cached mxc emotes as file:// with escaped path (TimelineModel.cpp:366-381); only the space bypass (I2) gets around it.

Room names and previews are escaped in the model (RoomModel.cpp:100,107); preview_sender in RoomDelegate.qml:301; MembersPage.qml:110; ThreadsPage.qml:44; reaction labels (TimelineModel.cpp:446); thread line (:198-200); emote body (:170).

call-bridge.js message listener checks `e.origin !== ORIGIN` (:103), polyfill only into ORIGIN windows (:94), and posts to the page with targetOrigin ORIGIN (:124): another page cannot talk to the widget driver through postMessage.
SSO: Rustrx adds only the open_url hop; the localhost listener and the login token stay in the SDK (session.rs:414-429); nothing logs the URL or the token.
ShareAdaptor names go through QFileInfo(name).fileName() (:79, :94): no path traversal out of cache/shared.

Push payload: room and event ids are parsed by OwnedRoomId/OwnedEventId::try_from in push.rs:77-78 before use; the connector checks the token (but see I10 for the empty-token case); the endpoint must be https (UnifiedPush.cpp:293-297).

The notification text setting is honoured on both message paths: Service.qml:99 (sync) and :224 (push); the cover too (CoverPage.qml:155). Invitation, call and knock banners carry names regardless, by design (no message text).

Core logging: all 72 tracing calls in core/src carry ids, counts, timings or error text; no body, password, recovery key, token or endpoint. The C++ command log line carries only the command name (Rustrx.cpp:379-383); the push endpoint is logged by size (UnifiedPush.cpp:301); session.json is written 0600 and atomically (session.rs:152-168).
push_handle's classic path checks only Mute (push.rs:111-113), but the homeserver pushes only events its push rules mark notify, so mentions-only rooms are already filtered server side.
openMatrixUri sends rooms and aliases to JoinPage, which asks before joining; only users skip the question (I5).
dev() refuses everything without the flag file, and no package installs it (Rustrx.cpp:327-331).

dead_ends: Looked for a SyncService hook that re-enables send queues on reconnect (matrix-sdk-ui 0.19.1 sync_service.rs): there is none; the only SDK caller of set_enabled(true) is Client::resume (client/mod.rs:3840).
Checked whether RoomSendQueueHandle::abort or unwedge re-enable the queue: both only notify (send_queue/mod.rs:2864, 2883, 3012); only set_enabled stores true (mod.rs:1233).

Checked whether login can overlap restore at boot: the UI only shows the login page after ready logged_in:false, and the buttons are disabled while loggingIn (LoginPage.qml:117, 173, 202); the double-login race the first audit named needs a direct D-Bus/dev command, so it is folded into C2/C8 rather than reported alone.
Checked open_room vs close_room for the C7 race: possible but narrow, the live-focus timeline build is mostly local; reported under C7 only as the narrow case.

Checked the NotificationClient for cross-instance exclusion: its encryption_sync_mutex and permit are per instance (notification_client.rs:336-343); the multi-process lock uses one shared LOCK_ID, so instances in one process do not exclude each other (C6). Not run.
Qt 5.6's moment of closing the session bus connection (QGuiApplication destruction vs exit) was not verified; C9 stays SUSPECTED either way because the tokio runtime outlives both.
sailfish-secrets behaviour before the first unlock (blocks vs returns an error) was not verified; C3 and C12 cover the two outcomes.
QML 'Send again' for media is hidden (MessageDelegate.qml:724); a failed upload can only be discarded, which hits the same disabled queue (C1).

matrix-sdk 0.19 sources are not on this machine (no cargo registry; builds run on e15), so what the SDK itself logs at WARN (the default filter) was not read; a run with the default filter and a grep of the log for bodies is the way to check.
Qt StyledText behaviour was read from the qtdeclarative 5.6 branch (GitHub raw) and the local 6.11.3 source; not reproduced on a phone with Qt 5.6.3.

Not checked: whether sailfish-browser hands a matrix: link to Rustrx without a prompt (decides how easy I5 is from the web); whether lipstick renders notification bodies as rich text (would carry I1 into the notification server); what Qt.openUrlExternally(file://...) opens from inside sailjail (decides the impact of I3).
